NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI accelerator value chain, acting as a fabless semiconductor designer that is critically dependent on TSMC for cutting-edge chip fabrication and SK Hynix for HBM memory, giving it a highly concentrated but high-quality upstream supply base. On the downstream side, NVIDIA's revenue is dominated by a small group of hyperscale cloud providers (Microsoft, Meta, Google, Amazon) who are racing to build AI infrastructure, creating both massive demand tailwinds and customer concentration risk.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the premium end of the consumer electronics value chain, acting as a powerful systems integrator that designs its own silicon but relies heavily on TSMC for fabrication and a concentrated group of Asian suppliers for displays, memory, and components. On the downstream side, Apple sells primarily through carrier partners and its own retail/online channels, with its high-margin Services segment increasingly dependent on platform relationships — most notably its lucrative search deal with Google — making it both a hardware distributor and a digital platform gatekeeper.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits at the heart of the global memory supply chain, transforming raw silicon wafers and advanced semiconductor equipment inputs from a concentrated set of capital equipment and materials suppliers into DRAM and NAND products that are indispensable to cloud hyperscalers, AI accelerator vendors, mobile OEMs, and automotive manufacturers. Its strategic position is increasingly critical as AI workloads drive surging demand for High Bandwidth Memory, though it remains heavily dependent on a small number of lithography and equipment suppliers, creating meaningful concentration risk on the upstream side.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: Arm Holdings sits at the intellectual property layer of the global semiconductor ecosystem, licensing CPU and GPU architecture designs rather than manufacturing physical chips, making it a capital-light but strategically critical node between EDA tool providers upstream and virtually every major chip designer downstream. Its royalty and licensing revenue model means its financial performance is directly tied to the volume and value of chips shipped by licensees — spanning mobile, cloud, automotive, and IoT — giving it unparalleled breadth of downstream exposure across the semiconductor value chain.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology is a fabless semiconductor company occupying a critical middle position in the data infrastructure supply chain, sourcing advanced chip fabrication almost exclusively from TSMC and licensed IP from Arm while selling custom ASICs, networking silicon, and storage controllers to hyperscale cloud providers and enterprise OEMs. Its strategic pivot toward custom AI silicon for major cloud players (Amazon, Google, Microsoft) has made these hyperscalers increasingly dominant in its revenue mix, with data center now representing over 70% of total revenue.
